title: Two men sentenced after CBSA officers stopped an illegal crossing in Manitoba
orig_title: Two men sentenced after CBSA officers stopped an illegal crossing in Manitoba
summary: Two people have been sentenced over an illegal border crossing at the Sprague crossing in Manitoba. The Canada Border Services Agency said it stopped a minivan on May 7 because of "inconsistencies" in the driver's declaration, and officers found a 46-year-old man hiding in the trunk. That man, Temitope Omofuyi Davies, told officers he had paid the driver $1,000 to get him into Canada, and the agency later learned he had also been caught trying to cross near Surrey, B.C., in March. Davies pleaded guilty to failure to report on Aug. 19 and was sentenced to time served. The driver, Annan Nigel Ferguson, a 50-year-old American citizen, was sentenced on Nov. 4 to one year in prison for aiding and abetting failure to report. With time served counted, he has roughly three months left on the sentence.

orig_title: Effort to get trucks off Van Dam in Saratoga Springs continues to stall
summary:
Saratoga Springs residents and city officials are again pushing to move tractor-trailer traffic off Van Dam Street. The push followed a late-night crash between a Skidmore College bus and a tractor-trailer that blocked traffic for hours at Van Dam and Clinton streets, though no major injuries occurred.

A five-ton weight limit ordinance the City Council passed in December 2023 came down within days, because the state said city officials had no authority to pass local ordinances on the state-designated route. A city request for a traffic study outlined rerouting trucks via Route 9 from Northway exit 14 in Malta or via Route 50 through Ballston Spa. The state said de-designating a route requires documented operational deficiencies or a provable history of accidents. A neighborhood association study counted upward of 700 trucks a day, and the Trucking Association of New York warned that de-designation could push trucks onto other routes.
